newsitem.title: UK: Guardian H1 profits expected to slip.
newsitem.headline: Guardian H1 profits expected to slip.

text.p: Guardian Royal Exchange Plc kicks off the half year reporting season among insurers next Wednesday, with attention likely to centre on the group's future strategy.
At the annual results in February, GRE dismissed the possibility of using excess capital to buy-back shares and instead said it planned to spend up to 1.25 billion stg on an acquisition.
Topping its wish-list was a life company but it also declared itself keen to expand in non-life lines in the UK and U.S.
Worries about a big acquisition, and the goodwill write-off a life acquisition would require, have tended to overhang the shares.
But some analysts suggest such a move is looking less probable.
"A large acquistion looks extremely unlikely. There's nothing out there to buy," said one.
Another analyst suggested GRE may decide to focus attention on the health sector.
"That would probably be a positive for the shares. It's harder to spend a lot of money in the health sector," he added.
For the first half, analysts expect another fall in operating profits, with the difficult rating environment continuing to hold back results.
Pre-tax trading profit forecasts range between 110 and 130 million stg, down from 137 million stg last year.
The dividend is expected to rise to around 3.75 pence and net asset value is forecast at between 318 and 330 pence per share.
At the annual meeting in April GRE described trading in the first three months of 1997 as 'satisfactory' and chairman Lord Hambro said the group had a 'clear strategy for the future'.
Confirming it intended to expand the life and health insurance business both organically and by acquisition, Hambro stressed the company would not be tempted to pay too much for any purchase.
No dramatic news on rates is expected next week and one analyst suggested that the focus across the sector was more likely to be on capital issues.

"The market isn't really fixated with trading results but on the size of the balance sheets these companies have and the difficulty of getting good returns on capital when they're over-capitalised," said the analyst.
At the annual results GRE forecast an 8.0 percent rise across the board in UK personal motor rates in 1997 - the biggest rise in six years - and a 2-3 percent increase in household rates.
Progress at Guardian Direct, the group's telephone-based motor insurance arm, is also likely to attract attention.
At year-end GRE said it expected to break-even this year and the group expects to be in Britain's top three within the next two years.
Internationally the key area is Germany.
Rates are under pressure there generally but claims experience remains quite good and industry ananlysts will be looking to see how those factors are playing out.
Sterling's strength will have an effect there and the market will want more details about the company's exposure to recent flooding.
The U.S. and Canada are expected to show a weather-related rebound after the severe conditions of last year.
In 1996 annual profits for the group fell 17 percent to 281 million stg as fierce UK competition and the worst weather claims in the U.S. for 75 years hit results.
Adverse weather and subsidence costs in the UK were also factors.
-- Simon Cowell, London Newsroom +44 171 542 7721
